questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: trade between people of different lands has been happening for thousands of years.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: True. Mapungubwe traded across the Indian Ocean 800 years ago. Egyptian merchants reached central Africa thousands of years ago. Trade is as old as people meeting people.

questions.question: Which is a CONSEQUENCE of unfair trade for farmers?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is one consequence of unfair trade for farmers?
options: Farmers stay poor even when the world buys lots of their crops
questions.expected: Farmers stay poor even when the world buys lots of their crops
questions.memo: A cocoa farmer in West Africa might earn very little even though chocolate is a multi-billion dollar industry. Their work feeds the world; their pay doesn't reflect that.

questions.question: Tell me ONE thing your family BUYS that came from another country.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one thing your family buys that probably came from another country.
questions.expected: My cell phone came from China
questions.memo: Good answers: cell phone (often China), TV, certain food (chocolate, coffee, tea), petrol (oil from many places), cars, clothes. All real imports.

questions.question: Which BEST sums up what TRADE is about?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which best sums up what trade is about?
options: Exchanging what we make for what we need — and doing it as fairly as possible
questions.expected: Exchanging what we make for what we need — and doing it as fairly as possible
questions.memo: Trade is human cooperation across distance. Done fairly, it helps everyone. Done unfairly, it deepens poverty. We can choose what kind of trade to support.

SS.L6.GEO.T03.title: Climate and vegetation around the world
SS.L6.GEO.T03.description: Hot, mild and cold climates; tropical rainforests; hot deserts; coniferous forests — climate, vegetation, wildlife and how people live in each.
SS.L6.GEO.T03.recovery_strategy: Different climates create different worlds. Rainforests: hot + wet + thick trees. Deserts: hot + dry + few plants. Coniferous forests: cold + tall needle-leaved trees. Climate shapes plants, animals AND people.

questions.question: Why are climates DIFFERENT in different parts of the world?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is the climate different in different parts of the world?
options: The sun heats some parts more than others, and oceans, wind and height also affect climate
questions.expected: The sun heats some parts more than others, and oceans, wind and height also affect climate
questions.memo: Near the equator = most heat from the sun. Near the poles = least. Mountains are cold. Coasts and inland areas differ. Many factors together create climate.

questions.question: Which climate zone is near the EQUATOR?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which climate zone is near the equator?
questions.expected: Hot tropical climate
questions.memo: The equator gets the most direct sunlight all year. Areas there are HOT — like the rainforests of central Africa, the Amazon and Southeast Asia.

questions.question: What is a TROPICAL RAINFOREST?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is a tropical rainforest?
options: A hot, very wet forest near the equator with thick, tall trees
questions.expected: A hot, very wet forest near the equator with thick, tall trees
questions.memo: Rainforests are warm AND wet all year. The Amazon and Congo are the biggest. They contain most of the world's plant and animal species.

questions.question: Which famous rainforest is in AFRICA?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which famous rainforest is in Africa?
questions.expected: The Congo Rainforest
questions.memo: The Congo Basin holds the second largest rainforest in the world (after the Amazon). Gorillas, okapi and forest elephants live there.

questions.question: What is DEFORESTATION?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is deforestation?
options: Cutting down forests faster than they can grow back
questions.expected: Cutting down forests faster than they can grow back
questions.memo: Deforestation destroys habitat, releases carbon dioxide and removes biodiversity. Major problem for the Amazon and Congo rainforests.

questions.question: Why is rainforest deforestation a PROBLEM?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is cutting down rainforests a serious problem?
options: Loss of wildlife, loss of medicine plants, more carbon dioxide and climate change
questions.expected: Loss of wildlife, loss of medicine plants, more carbon dioxide and climate change
questions.memo: Rainforests are like lungs — they breathe in carbon dioxide and breathe out oxygen. Destroy them and the whole world feels it.

questions.question: What is a HOT DESERT?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is a hot desert?
options: A very dry area with little rainfall and few plants — but often very hot in the day
questions.expected: A very dry area with little rainfall and few plants — but often very hot in the day
questions.memo: Less than 250mm of rain per year = desert. The Sahara, Namib and Australian outback are hot deserts. Cold nights, hot days.

questions.question: Which is AFRICA's biggest desert?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is Africa's biggest desert?
questions.expected: The Sahara, in northern Africa
questions.memo: The Sahara covers most of northern Africa — bigger than the entire USA. Mostly sand, rocks and dunes, with scattered oases of green.

questions.question: Which is a desert plant?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which plant is well-suited to a desert?
options: The cactus — thick stem stores water, spines reduce water loss
questions.expected: The cactus — thick stem stores water, spines reduce water loss
questions.memo: Desert plants adapt by storing water (cactus), having waxy or tiny leaves, or going dormant when dry. Survival means saving water.

questions.question: How do PEOPLE often live in HOT DESERTS?
questions.ruby_prompt: How do people often live in hot deserts?
options: Many are nomadic — moving with animals; or they live near oases and rivers
questions.expected: Many are nomadic — moving with animals; or they live near oases and rivers
questions.memo: Bedouins in the Sahara, Tuareg in the Sahel — nomadic peoples who move with their herds. Others cluster around oases or the Nile.

questions.question: What is a CONIFEROUS FOREST?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is a coniferous forest?
options: A forest of tall trees with needle leaves and cones — found in cold areas like Canada and Russia
questions.expected: A forest of tall trees with needle leaves and cones — found in cold areas like Canada and Russia
questions.memo: Conifers like pine, spruce and fir thrive in cold places. They keep their needles year-round and grow tall. Huge belt across northern Canada, Scandinavia, Russia.

questions.question: Why do CONIFER trees have NEEDLE-LIKE leaves?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do conifers have needle-like leaves?
options: Needles lose less water and survive cold and snow better
questions.expected: Needles lose less water and survive cold and snow better
questions.memo: Needles are tough and waxy — they survive cold and reduce water loss. They can keep working through winter, so conifers stay green.

questions.question: Which animal lives in CONIFEROUS forests?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which animal might you find in coniferous forests?
questions.expected: Bears, moose, wolves and reindeer
questions.memo: Coniferous forests support large mammals adapted to cold. They have thick fur, store fat for winter, and some hibernate or migrate.

questions.question: How do PEOPLE often make a living in coniferous forest areas?
questions.ruby_prompt: How do people often make a living in coniferous forest areas?
options: Logging, hunting, fishing, fur trade and forest work
questions.expected: Logging, hunting, fishing, fur trade and forest work
questions.memo: Forests provide wood for timber and paper. Many communities in Russia, Scandinavia and Canada have worked in forests for generations.

questions.question: Put these climates in order — HOTTEST to COLDEST.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these climates in order from hottest to coldest.
questions.expected: Tropical rainforest (hot, wet),Hot desert (hot, dry),Temperate (mild),Coniferous forest (cold)
questions.memo: Rainforests and deserts are both HOT but very different in rainfall. Temperate (like Cape Town) is mild. Coniferous forests are cold.

questions.question: Which climate has WET summers AND wet winters?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which climate is wet all year — wet summers AND wet winters?
questions.expected: Tropical rainforest
questions.memo: Rainforests get rain in EVERY month. That's why everything grows so much and so fast. No real dry season.

questions.question: True or false: People who live in DESERTS often wear LIGHT, LOOSE clothing.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: people who live in hot deserts often wear light, loose clothing that covers most of the body.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: True. Light colours reflect sun, loose clothing allows air movement, covering skin protects from sun and dust. Smart adaptation to a tough climate.

questions.question: Why do different CLIMATES grow different PLANTS?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do different climates grow different kinds of plants?
options: Each plant has evolved for certain rainfall, temperature and seasons
questions.expected: Each plant has evolved for certain rainfall, temperature and seasons
questions.memo: A cactus would die in the Amazon — too wet. A rainforest tree would die in the Sahara — too dry. Plants are matched to their climate over millions of years.

questions.question: Tell me ONE way climate affects HUMAN LIFE.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one way climate affects how humans live.
questions.expected: Climate affects what crops we can grow
questions.memo: Good answers: food we grow, clothes we wear, houses we build, jobs available, how we travel, how we celebrate, when we plant and harvest. All real.

questions.question: Which BEST sums up climate and vegetation around the world?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which best sums up climate and vegetation around the world?
options: Climate shapes the plants, the animals AND the people who live in each region
questions.expected: Climate shapes the plants, the animals AND the people who live in each region
questions.memo: It's a chain: climate → plants → animals (that eat the plants) → people (who depend on both). Change one and the whole chain feels it.

SS.L6.GEO.T04.title: Population — why people live where they do
SS.L6.GEO.T04.description: Population distribution and density in SA and the world; reasons for settlement; rural vs urban; rural-to-urban migration.
SS.L6.GEO.T04.recovery_strategy: People settle where life is EASIER — water, good climate, jobs, safety. Cities pull people from the countryside because there's more work. Rural = countryside, urban = city.

questions.question: What does 'POPULATION' mean?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does population mean?
options: The total number of people living in a place
questions.expected: The total number of people living in a place
questions.memo: Population is the total people count. South Africa's population is about 60 million. Some provinces have many more than others.

questions.question: What does 'POPULATION DENSITY' mean?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does population density mean?
options: How CROWDED a place is — number of people per area of land
questions.expected: How CROWDED a place is — number of people per area of land
questions.memo: A small province with many people = high density. A big province with few people = low density. Both can have the same total population.

questions.question: Which is South Africa's most populated province?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is South Africa's most populated province?
questions.expected: Gauteng
questions.memo: Gauteng — South Africa's smallest province by area, but home to about 15 million people. Johannesburg and Pretoria are both here.

questions.question: Which is South Africa's LEAST populated province?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is South Africa's least populated province?
questions.expected: Northern Cape
questions.memo: Northern Cape is huge (the biggest by area) but mostly desert/Karoo. Few people, far apart. Lowest population density.

questions.question: Why might MANY people live near a RIVER or COAST?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why might many people live near rivers or coasts?
options: Water for drinking, farming, fishing, and easier trade by boat
questions.expected: Water for drinking, farming, fishing, and easier trade by boat
questions.memo: Water is life and trade. Most of the world's biggest cities are coastal or on rivers — Cape Town, Durban, London, Cairo, Mumbai.

questions.question: Why do FEW people live in DESERTS?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do few people live in deserts?
options: Very little water, harsh heat, hard to grow food
questions.expected: Very little water, harsh heat, hard to grow food
questions.memo: Without water and farmland, supporting many people is very hard. Desert populations are spread thin or cluster near oases.

questions.question: What does 'RURAL' mean?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does rural mean?
options: The countryside — small villages, farms, open land
questions.expected: The countryside — small villages, farms, open land
questions.memo: Rural areas have fewer people, more space, often more farming. Most South African provinces have large rural areas.

questions.question: What does 'URBAN' mean?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does urban mean?
options: Towns and cities — many people, buildings, shops, services
questions.expected: Towns and cities — many people, buildings, shops, services
questions.memo: Urban = city/town life. Jobs, schools, hospitals, shops nearby. Crowded but with more services.

questions.question: Why do people MIGRATE from rural areas to cities?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do people move from the countryside to cities?
options: For jobs, education, health care and better services
questions.expected: For jobs, education, health care and better services
questions.memo: Rural → urban migration happens worldwide. Cities offer hope of better income and a chance for children. But cities also struggle to handle the growth.

questions.question: What is a CHALLENGE of rural-to-urban migration?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is a challenge that comes with many people moving to cities?
options: Cities can become overcrowded; informal settlements form; services are stretched
questions.expected: Cities can become overcrowded; informal settlements form; services are stretched
questions.memo: When growth is faster than housing and jobs, problems follow: shacks, unemployment, traffic, water shortages. SA cities deal with this every day.

questions.question: Which is a major South African city?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a major South African city?
options: Johannesburg, Cape Town, Durban, Pretoria, Port Elizabeth (Gqeberha)
questions.expected: Johannesburg, Cape Town, Durban, Pretoria, Port Elizabeth (Gqeberha)
questions.memo: These are SA's biggest cities. Johannesburg around gold, Cape Town and Durban around ports, Pretoria as the administrative capital.

questions.question: Why did JOHANNESBURG grow so fast?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why did Johannesburg grow so fast?
options: Gold was discovered there in 1886 — people flooded in for mining work
questions.expected: Gold was discovered there in 1886 — people flooded in for mining work
questions.memo: Joburg went from open veld to a big city in just a few decades — entirely because of gold. The city was built by miners from all over Southern Africa and beyond.

questions.question: Why do MANY people live in CAPE TOWN?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do many people live in Cape Town?
options: A natural harbour, mild climate, jobs, beauty and centuries of settlement
questions.expected: A natural harbour, mild climate, jobs, beauty and centuries of settlement
questions.memo: Cape Town has many pulls: a port, mild winters, beauty (Table Mountain), a long history, varied work. It keeps growing year on year.

questions.question: Which factor LIMITS where people can live in WORLD?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which factor most limits where people can live in the world?
questions.expected: Lack of fresh water
questions.memo: Water above all. Cities can solve most problems — but without water nothing works. Cape Town's recent water crisis showed how serious this can get.

questions.question: True or false: People live in nearly EVERY part of the earth.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: people live in nearly every part of the earth.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: True. From the Arctic to the equator, from islands to mountains, people have adapted. Only Antarctica has no permanent residents.

questions.question: Which is a major world city with HUGE population?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a major world city with a huge population?
options: Tokyo, Shanghai, Lagos, Mumbai or Mexico City
questions.expected: Tokyo, Shanghai, Lagos, Mumbai or Mexico City
questions.memo: Each of these has over 20 million people. The world is becoming more URBAN every year. Most of humanity now lives in cities.

questions.question: Put these in order — reasons people settled in a place.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order — the reasons people choose to settle somewhere.
options: Water available for drinking and farming
Climate good enough to live and grow food
questions.expected: Water available for drinking and farming,Climate good enough to live and grow food,Safety and resources (other materials, jobs),Connections — roads, ports, neighbours
questions.memo: Water first. Then food possibility. Then safety + resources. Then connections to others. Every long-lasting settlement has these.

questions.question: True or false: South Africa was once VERY UNFAIR in deciding WHERE people could live (by race).
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: in the past, South African laws were very unfair — telling people where they could live based on their race.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: True. Apartheid laws forced millions of people off their land into rural 'homelands' or specific townships. The effects are still seen in SA's geography today.

questions.question: Tell me ONE reason your family lives WHERE you live.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one reason your family lives where you live.
questions.expected: My family lives here because my parents work in this area
questions.memo: Good answers: work, family, history, schools, safety, affordable housing, close to relatives, born here. All valid.

questions.question: Which BEST sums up why people live WHERE they do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which best sums up why people live where they do?
options: A combination of geography (water, climate), history, jobs and family — different in every place
questions.expected: A combination of geography (water, climate), history, jobs and family — different in every place
questions.memo: Geography sets the basics. History (good and bad) shapes who is where. Jobs decide who can stay. Family is a strong pull. Every person's story combines all four.
